subject: Post-demo parity & hallucination eval — proposed test roadmap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@cloudpeak.ai>, Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@cloudpeak.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo parity & hallucination eval — proposed test roadmap

Alex / Sana — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and an actionable test plan so we keep momentum while you run the internal procurement checks.

Recap (high level)
- You asked for an apples-to-apples comparison vs the hyperscaler endpoint (latency+cost) and, critically, model output parity for your assistant flows (customer support + policy response).
- You emphasized hallucination rates and deterministic failure modes matter most for your compliance team.
- Procurement requested a short mutual-action-plan and a concrete evaluation artifact that their security and procurement teams can attach to the RFP.

Proposed next steps (timeline in parentheses):
1) Parity test suite delivery (3 business days) — we’ll share a curated set of 200 prompts and golden responses representative of your support & policy intents.
2) Hallucination probe matrix (3 business days) — prioritize categories you called out: product specs, refund policy, PII redaction, multi-step reasoning.
3) Live API parity run (2 business days) — side-by-side calls: CloudPeak-hyperscaler vs Redwood-hosted model variants (same base model family, quantized and FP16). We’ll capture per-token latencies, tail p99, and cost-per-100k-tokens estimates.
4) Regression checklist and alert criteria (1 business day) — thresholds for hallucination delta, semantic match, and BLEU/ROUGE style similarity metrics; recommendations for fallback routing.

Attachments: parity-hallucination-matrix.xlsx (matrix with categories, severity, test prompts), sample-prompts-and-golden-responses.jsonl (subset)

Ask: Can you confirm the 200-prompt coverage is acceptable and whether we should prioritize support or policy for the first run? Also, share an internal contact for procurement so we can include the evaluation artifacts in the RFP package.

If that looks good, Rishi will run the comparison and Ben will own cost modeling and the SLI/SLO notes. I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a short 30-min alignment sync.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192


-----Original Message-----

Thanks Jordan — that plan looks solid. A few clarifications from our side: we absolutely need the fidelity checks on policy flows first (legal wants to see those). For latency, we care most about 99th percentile under our typical burst profile (50 concurrent users). Also, procurement will want a consumable artifact they can attach to a security review — does your parity matrix include data handling and KV-cache behavior notes?

Procurement contact: procurement@cloudpeak.ai
Legal contact for policy questions: legal@cloudpeak.ai

We’ll also need cost guidance for both dedicated and hosted modes — our infra team likes to see committed vs burst costs side-by-side.

—Alex
Alex Sanders
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships | CloudPeak AI
alex.sanders@cloudpeak.ai


On Sep 14, 2028, at 16:05, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

> Jordan / Alex / Sana — adding the technical plan. I attached an initial parity matrix and a small sample prompt set (first 30 prompts) so CloudPeak can sanity-check coverage. High-level approach below.
> 
> Approach:
> - Test harness: we will run each prompt 5 times against each endpoint to capture variability (deterministic seeds where supported).
> - Metrics: semantic similarity (embedding cosine + threshold), hallucination flag (binary based on golden response diff), top-token overlap, answer length, and p99 latency under batch sizes 1 and 8.
> - Models: we’ll match model family (e.g., LlamaX-13B equivalent) and run both quantized and FP16 variants; Redwood will also test our cache-enabled path to show reductions in per-token compute for repeated prefixes.
> - Failure modes to instrument: policy contradictions, hallucinated factual claims (dates/URLs), incorrect enumerations, and PII leakage.
> 
> Deliverables (internal ownership):
> - parity-hallucination-matrix.xlsx — full prompt set mapping to categories (me)
> - sample-prompts-and-golden-responses.jsonl — canonical answers (Marissa will curate)
> - runbook + scripts — reproducible harness in a shared Drive (Ben will share cost script)
> 
> Timeline: I can start runs tomorrow (Fri) if CloudPeak signs off on the 30-sample coverage and confirms policy-first priority. Expect preliminary artifacts by Monday EOD.
> 
> Attachment: parity-hallucination-matrix.xlsx (see tab1 for prompt categories)
> 
> Rishi
> Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
> rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
